records.source: אָ֣ז יָשִֽׁיר־מֹשֶׁה֩ וּבְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־הַשִּׁירָ֤ה הַזֹּאת֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֵאמֹ֑ר אָשִׁ֤ירָה לַֽיהוָה֙ כִּֽי־גָאֹ֣ה גָּאָ֔ה ס֥וּס וְרֹכְב֖וֹ רָמָ֥ה בַיָּֽם׃
records.gloss: Then sang Moses and [the] sons of Israel the song the this to Yahweh, and they said, saying, I will sing to Yahweh, for highly he is exalted; horse and its rider he has thrown in [the] sea.
pieces: Then Moses and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} sang this song to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: "I will sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is lifted high in triumph; horse and rider {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has flung into the sea.

L.1: Then Moses and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel sang this song to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they said, "I will sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for highly exalted is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}; horse and its rider {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has cast into the sea.

R.1: Then Moses and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} sang this song to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: "I will sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has won a great victory. He threw the horses and their riders into the sea.

decisions.choice: then: at that time, when Israel had seen the dead Egyptians and believed (14:30-31)
decisions.reason: The song answers what chapter 14 tells. The verb "sang" is singular, with Moses first, though the people sing with him. Verses 1-18 are a poem.

decisions.choice: highly exalted: he has risen up in majesty, he has triumphed
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for force. It means to rise up high, and so to show oneself majestic and victorious. The same words open Miriam's refrain in verse 21.

decisions.choice: horse and its rider: Pharaoh's horses and the men they carried
decisions.reason: The singular stands for the whole force. Chapter 14 speaks of horses, chariots and horsemen (14:9, 23), so the "rider" may be a horseman or the man driving a chariot.

decisions.choice: he has won a great victory
decisions.reason: Readable says what "highly exalted" means here: God has shown his greatness by defeating Egypt.

records.heading: The song of Moses

records.source: עָזִּ֤י וְזִמְרָת֙ יָ֔הּ וַֽיְהִי־לִ֖י לִֽישׁוּעָ֑ה זֶ֤ה אֵלִי֙ וְאַנְוֵ֔הוּ אֱלֹהֵ֥י אָבִ֖י וַאֲרֹמְמֶֽנְהוּ׃
records.gloss: My strength and [my] song [is] Yah, and he has become for me salvation. This [is] my God, and I will glorify him; [the] God of my father, and I will exalt him.
pieces: My strength and my song is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has come to save me. This is my God, and I will honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with praise; the God of my father, and I will lift {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} high.

L.2: My strength and song [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has become salvation for me. This [is] my God, and I will praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; [the] God of my father, and I will exalt {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.2: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yah}} makes me strong, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the reason for my song. He has rescued me. He is my God, and I will praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He is my father's God, and I will tell how great {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is.

decisions.choice: Yah: a short form of the divine name Yahweh
decisions.reason: The word is the first part of the name Yahweh, used mostly in poetry and in praise (17:16; Psalm 68:5; the "-iah" at the end of names such as Isaiah). It means the same God as the full name.

decisions.choice: song: the song of praise sung to him
decisions.reason: The word most often means song or music. A word spelled the same way can mean strength, might or protection, which would pair with "my strength" ("my strength and my might"). The same line is repeated in Isaiah 12:2 and Psalm 118:14.

decisions.choice: I will praise him: I will give him honor and glory
alternatives: I will make him a dwelling
decisions.reason: The verb is rare. It most likely means to praise or adorn with praise, parallel with "I will exalt him". It has also been read as "I will make him a dwelling", from a word for an abode (verse 13).

decisions.choice: the LORD, with Yah as the alternative
decisions.reason: The short form is shown as "the LORD" like the full name. A reader who chooses the name sees "Yah", the form the Hebrew has here.

decisions.choice: has come to save me (Balanced); has rescued me (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 14:13, Balanced and Readable turn "salvation" into a verb. Literal keeps "salvation".

records.source: יְהוָ֖ה אִ֣ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֑ה יְהוָ֖ה שְׁמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Yahweh [is] a man of war; Yahweh [is] his name.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is a man of war; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] a man of war; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

R.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} fights like a soldier in battle. His name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a man of war: a warrior
decisions.reason: "Man of war" means a fighting man, a soldier (Joshua 17:1; 1 Samuel 17:33). Israel did not fight; Yahweh fought for them, as Moses promised (14:14, 25).

decisions.choice: Yahweh is his name: his name tells who he is
decisions.reason: The name God made known to Moses (3:14-15; 6:2-3) is now known by what he has done. The Egyptians and Israel have learned that he is Yahweh (14:18).

decisions.choice: fights like a soldier in battle
decisions.reason: Readable says what "man of war" means.

records.source: מַרְכְּבֹ֥ת פַּרְעֹ֛ה וְחֵיל֖וֹ יָרָ֣ה בַיָּ֑ם וּמִבְחַ֥ר שָֽׁלִשָׁ֖יו טֻבְּע֥וּ בְיַם־סֽוּף׃
records.gloss: [The] chariots of Pharaoh and his army he has thrown in [the] sea, and [the] choicest of his officers have been sunk in [the] Sea of Reeds.
pieces: Pharaoh's chariots and his army {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has hurled into the sea; his finest officers went down in the Red Sea.

L.4: The chariots of Pharaoh and his army {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has thrown into the sea, and the choicest of his officers have been sunk in the Sea of Reeds.

R.4: He threw Pharaoh's chariots and his army into the sea. Pharaoh's best officers drowned in the Red Sea.

decisions.choice: the choicest of his officers: Pharaoh's picked chariot officers
decisions.reason: The word for officer is the one used in 14:7 for the officers over Pharaoh's chariots, perhaps the third man in a chariot.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Reeds: the sea of the crossing
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name is "Sea of Reeds", the name used for the sea of the crossing (13:18; 14). See the note at 10:19.

decisions.choice: the Red Sea
decisions.reason: As at 10:19, Balanced and Readable use the familiar name; Literal translates the Hebrew name, "Sea of Reeds".

records.source: תְּהֹמֹ֖ת יְכַסְיֻ֑מוּ יָרְד֥וּ בִמְצוֹלֹ֖ת כְּמוֹ־אָֽבֶן׃
records.gloss: [The] deeps cover them; they went down in [the] depths like a stone.
pieces: The deep waters closed over them; like a stone they dropped to the bottom.

L.5: The deeps cover them; they went down into the depths like a stone.

R.5: The deep water covered them. They sank to the bottom like a rock.

decisions.choice: the deeps: the deep waters of the sea
decisions.reason: The word is used of the deep waters of creation (Genesis 1:2) and of the flood (Genesis 7:11). It is used again in verse 8.

decisions.choice: cover them: the waters covered them
decisions.reason: Hebrew poetry often uses verb forms freely for time. The covering happened at the sea (14:28), and the song tells it as a scene still before the singer's eyes.

records.source: יְמִֽינְךָ֣ יְהוָ֔ה נֶאְדָּרִ֖י בַּכֹּ֑חַ יְמִֽינְךָ֥ יְהוָ֖ה תִּרְעַ֥ץ אוֹיֵֽב׃
records.gloss: Your right hand, O Yahweh, glorious in power; your right hand, O Yahweh, shatters [the] enemy.
pieces: O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand is splendid in power; O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand smashed the enemy.

L.6: Your right hand, O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, [is] glorious in power; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand, O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, shatters [the] enemy.

R.6: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand is great and powerful. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand crushed the enemy.

decisions.choice: your right hand: your power in action
decisions.reason: The right hand is the stronger hand, and stands for strength put to work (verse 12; Psalm 118:15-16). God's "strong hand" was promised in 3:19-20 and 6:1.

decisions.choice: glorious: majestic, splendid
decisions.reason: The form may describe the hand ("glorious in power") or address it. The word is used again of God in verse 11.

decisions.choice: O LORD placed first
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the call to God at the start of each line; Literal keeps it after "your right hand". Balanced and Readable tell the smashing of the enemy as past, since the song looks back on the sea.

records.source: וּבְרֹ֥ב גְּאוֹנְךָ֖ תַּהֲרֹ֣ס קָמֶ֑יךָ תְּשַׁלַּח֙ חֲרֹ֣נְךָ֔ יֹאכְלֵ֖מוֹ כַּקַּֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And in [the] greatness of your majesty you throw down those rising against you; you send out your burning anger; it consumes them like stubble.
pieces: In {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} surpassing majesty {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} tore down those who rose against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} let loose {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fury, and it burned them up like straw.

L.7: And in the greatness of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} majesty {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} threw down those who rose against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} burning anger; it consumed them like stubble.

R.7: With {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} defeated {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies. Your anger blazed out and burned them up like dry straw.

decisions.choice: those who rose against you: God's enemies
decisions.reason: Pharaoh rose against Israel, and in doing so against God (5:2). The song counts Israel's enemy as God's enemy.

decisions.choice: your burning anger consumed them like stubble: God's anger like fire
decisions.reason: God's anger is pictured as fire that burns dry stubble in a moment (Isaiah 5:24; 47:14). "Stubble" is the word used in 5:12, where Israel had to gather it for bricks.

decisions.choice: defeated your enemies
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plain sense of "threw down those who rose against you".

records.source: וּבְר֤וּחַ אַפֶּ֨יךָ֙ נֶ֣עֶרְמוּ מַ֔יִם נִצְּב֥וּ כְמוֹ־נֵ֖ד נֹזְלִ֑ים קָֽפְא֥וּ תְהֹמֹ֖ת בְּלֶב־יָֽם׃
records.gloss: And by [the] breath of your nostrils were piled up [the] waters; stood up like a heap [the] streams; congealed [the] deeps in [the] heart of [the] sea.
pieces: At the blast of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} nostrils the waters were piled high; the flowing waters stood upright in a heap, and the depths grew solid in the heart of the sea.

L.8: And by the blast of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} nostrils the waters were piled up; the streams stood up like a heap; the deeps grew firm in the heart of the sea.

R.8: You breathed out a great blast, and the water piled up. The moving water stood up straight in a heap. The deep water turned hard in the middle of the sea.

decisions.choice: the blast of your nostrils: the east wind of 14:21, as God's own breath
decisions.reason: The word means breath or wind. The narrative says a strong east wind drove the sea back (14:21); the song pictures that wind as the snorting breath of God's nostrils, a picture of his power and anger (2 Samuel 22:16; Psalm 18:16).

decisions.choice: stood up like a heap: the waters stood upright like a wall
decisions.reason: "Heap" is the word used of the Jordan standing still in Joshua 3:13, 16. The narrative says the waters were a wall on either side (14:22, 29).

decisions.choice: congealed: thickened, became firm
decisions.reason: The verb is used of milk curdling (Job 10:10). The deep water stood as if it had turned solid.

decisions.choice: You breathed out a great blast
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of God's breath but leaves out "nostrils", which reads oddly in plain English.

records.source: אָמַ֥ר אוֹיֵ֛ב אֶרְדֹּ֥ף אַשִּׂ֖יג אֲחַלֵּ֣ק שָׁלָ֑ל תִּמְלָאֵ֣מוֹ נַפְשִׁ֔י אָרִ֣יק חַרְבִּ֔י תּוֹרִישֵׁ֖מוֹ יָדִֽי׃
records.gloss: Said [the] enemy, I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide [the] plunder; will be filled with them my soul; I will draw my sword; will dispossess them my hand.
pieces: The enemy said, 'I will chase them and catch them; I will share out the loot and take my fill of them; I will draw my sword, and my hand will wipe them out.'

L.9: The enemy said, 'I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide [the] plunder; my appetite will be filled with them; I will draw my sword; my hand will dispossess them.'

R.9: The enemy said, 'I will chase them and catch them. I will divide up what I take from them, and I will get all I want. I will pull out my sword and destroy them with my own hand.'

decisions.choice: my appetite will be filled with them: I will have all I want of them
decisions.reason: The word often rendered "soul" here means desire or appetite. The enemy pictures himself gorging on Israel and their goods.

decisions.choice: will dispossess them: will destroy them, take what is theirs
decisions.reason: The verb means to take possession, and so to drive out or destroy. The same verb is used of Israel taking the land (Numbers 33:53).

decisions.choice: short boasts with no joining words
decisions.reason: The enemy's words come in quick, breathless verbs, six of them beginning with "I" or "my". The pride of the boast is answered in the next verse by a single breath of God.

records.source: נָשַׁ֥פְתָּ בְרוּחֲךָ֖ כִּסָּ֣מוֹ יָ֑ם צָֽלֲלוּ֙ כַּֽעוֹפֶ֔רֶת בְּמַ֖יִם אַדִּירִֽים׃
records.gloss: You blew with your breath; covered them [the] sea; they sank like lead in [the] waters mighty.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} breathed out, and the sea closed over them; they went down like lead in the powerful waters.

L.10: You blew with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} breath; [the] sea covered them; they sank like lead in mighty waters.

R.10: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} blew {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} breath, and the sea covered them. They sank like heavy lead in the deep, powerful water.

decisions.choice: your breath: God's breath, the wind
decisions.reason: The same word as "blast" in verse 8: breath or wind. One breath from God undoes the enemy's boast in verse 9.

decisions.choice: mighty: majestic, powerful
decisions.reason: The word is used of what is great and noble. The waters that obey God are too strong for Pharaoh's army.

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the contrast with the enemy's boast in verse 9.

records.source: מִֽי־כָמֹ֤כָה בָּֽאֵלִם֙ יְהוָ֔ה מִ֥י כָּמֹ֖כָה נֶאְדָּ֣ר בַּקֹּ֑דֶשׁ נוֹרָ֥א תְהִלֹּ֖ת עֹ֥שֵׂה פֶֽלֶא׃
records.gloss: Who [is] like you among the gods, O Yahweh? Who [is] like you, glorious in holiness, fearsome [in] praises, doing wonder[s]?
pieces: Among the gods, who compares with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}? Who is like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, splendid in holiness, fearsome in deeds of praise, doer of wonders?

L.11: Who [is] like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} among the gods, O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}? Who [is] like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, glorious in holiness, fearsome [in] praises, doing wonders?

R.11: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, is any of the gods like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}? Is anyone like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, so glorious and holy? Your mighty deeds fill people with awe and praise. You do amazing wonders.

decisions.choice: among the gods: the gods the nations worshiped
decisions.reason: The word is a plural of the word for god. The question is a way of saying that no god compares with Yahweh. He has just carried out judgment on all the gods of Egypt (12:12; Numbers 33:4). The words grant no power to those gods. The word could also mean mighty ones in general.

decisions.choice: fearsome in praises: awe-inspiring in the deeds for which he is praised
decisions.reason: "Praises" can mean the acts that call out praise. God is to be feared and praised for what he has done.

decisions.choice: doing wonders: working wonders
decisions.reason: The word for wonder is used of acts only God can do (Psalm 77:15). It sums up the plagues and the crossing (3:20).

decisions.choice: Your mighty deeds fill people with awe and praise
decisions.reason: Readable spells out "fearsome in praises" as a sentence of its own.

records.source: נָטִ֨יתָ֙ יְמִ֣ינְךָ֔ תִּבְלָעֵ֖מוֹ אָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: You stretched out your right hand; swallowed them [the] earth.
pieces: You reached out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand, and the ground swallowed them.

L.12: You stretched out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand; [the] earth swallowed them up.

R.12: You reached out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right hand, and the earth swallowed up {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies.

decisions.choice: the earth swallowed them: they went down to death
decisions.reason: "The earth" here may mean the ground or the world below, the place of the dead (compare Numbers 16:32-33, where the earth opens). The Egyptians drowned in the sea, so the line speaks of their going down to death.

decisions.choice: your enemies
decisions.reason: Readable names whom the earth swallowed.

records.source: נָחִ֥יתָ בְחַסְדְּךָ֖ עַם־ז֣וּ גָּאָ֑לְתָּ נֵהַ֥לְתָּ בְעָזְּךָ֖ אֶל־נְוֵ֥ה קָדְשֶֽׁךָ׃
records.gloss: You led in your covenant loyalty [the] people which you redeemed; you guided [them] by your strength to [the] abode of your holiness.
pieces: With faithful love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} led the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had redeemed; with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strength {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} guided them on to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy abode.

L.13: You led in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} steadfast love [the] people that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} redeemed; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} guided [them] by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strength to the abode of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holiness.

R.13: Because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} led the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had set free. With {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strength, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} guided them to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy home.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyal, faithful love that keeps covenant
decisions.reason: This is the first time the word appears in Exodus. It means kindness that is owed and freely given within a bond: love that stays loyal to a promise and acts on it. God shows it to those he has bound himself to (20:6; 34:6-7; Genesis 24:27). Here it is the faithfulness to his promise to Abraham (2:24; 6:4-5) that led him to bring Israel out.

decisions.choice: redeemed: set free, as a kinsman frees his family
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a relative who buys back or frees a family member (Leviticus 25:25, 48). God promised to redeem Israel "with an outstretched arm" (6:6).

decisions.choice: your holy abode: the place where God dwells, and where he brings his people
decisions.reason: The word means a dwelling, often a pasture or settled home. It may mean Mount Sinai, where God meets Israel (3:12), or the land and the sanctuary of verse 17. The verbs may also look ahead, telling what God is sure to do.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal uses "steadfast love", and Balanced and Readable "faithful love"; both stress loyalty. Words such as "mercy" or "kindness" leave out the loyalty the word carries.

decisions.choice: set free
decisions.reason: Readable says what redeeming meant for Israel here: being set free from slavery. Literal and Balanced say "redeemed".

records.source: שָֽׁמְע֥וּ עַמִּ֖ים יִרְגָּז֑וּן חִ֣יל אָחַ֔ז יֹשְׁבֵ֖י פְּלָֽשֶׁת׃
records.gloss: Have heard peoples; they tremble; anguish has seized [the] inhabitants of Philistia.
pieces: Nations heard and shuddered; agony took hold of those who lived in Philistia.

L.14: Peoples heard; they trembled; writhing seized [the] inhabitants of Philistia.

R.14: Other nations heard what happened, and they shook with fear. The people of Philistia were in agony.

decisions.choice: the nations heard and trembled: what is sure to happen, told as done
alternatives: the nations will hear and tremble
decisions.reason: Verses 14-16 name peoples Israel will meet on the way to Canaan. The verbs may tell what happened when the news spread (Joshua 2:9-11), or speak of what is sure to come as if it had already happened.

decisions.choice: writhing: pain like a woman's labor
decisions.reason: The word is used of the pains of childbirth (Jeremiah 6:24). It pictures fear that grips the whole body.

decisions.choice: Philistia: the coast southwest of Canaan
decisions.reason: The land of the Philistines on the coast, along the road God did not lead Israel by (13:17).

decisions.choice: Other ... what happened
decisions.reason: Readable says what the nations heard.

records.source: אָ֤ז נִבְהֲלוּ֙ אַלּוּפֵ֣י אֱד֔וֹם אֵילֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב יֹֽאחֲזֵ֖מוֹ רָ֑עַד נָמֹ֕גוּ כֹּ֖ל יֹשְׁבֵ֥י כְנָֽעַן׃
records.gloss: Then are terrified [the] chiefs of Edom; [the] leaders of Moab, seizes them trembling; melted away all [the] inhabitants of Canaan.
pieces: Then Edom's clan chiefs were struck with dismay; Moab's rulers were gripped with trembling; everyone living in Canaan lost heart.

L.15: Then the chiefs of Edom were terrified; [as for the] leaders of Moab, trembling seized them; all [the] inhabitants of Canaan melted away.

R.15: The leaders of Edom were terrified. The rulers of Moab shook with fear. All the people of Canaan lost their courage.

decisions.choice: chiefs ... leaders: clan chiefs of Edom, the rulers of Moab
decisions.reason: The word for Edom's chiefs is used of the heads of Esau's clans (Genesis 36:15-19). The word for Moab's leaders means rams, a picture of strong leaders.

decisions.choice: melted away: lost all courage
decisions.reason: Hearts that melt are hearts that lose courage (Joshua 2:9, 11; 5:1).

decisions.choice: Edom, Moab, Canaan: the peoples on Israel's way to the promised land
decisions.reason: Edom and Moab lay south and east of the Dead Sea, and Israel passed by them (Numbers 20-21). Canaan is the land promised to the fathers (6:4).

decisions.choice: lost heart (Balanced); lost their courage (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "melted away" means.

records.source: תִּפֹּ֨ל עֲלֵיהֶ֤ם אֵימָ֨תָה֙ וָפַ֔חַד בִּגְדֹ֥ל זְרוֹעֲךָ֖ יִדְּמ֣וּ כָּאָ֑בֶן עַד־יַעֲבֹ֤ר עַמְּךָ֙ יְהוָ֔ה עַֽד־יַעֲבֹ֖ר עַם־ז֥וּ קָנִֽיתָ׃
records.gloss: Falls on them terror and dread; by [the] greatness of your arm they are still like stone, until passes over your people, O Yahweh, until passes over [the] people which you acquired.
pieces: Fear and dread came down on them; at the might of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arm they stood silent as stone, while {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people crossed over, O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, while the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own crossed over.

L.16: Terror and dread fell on them; by the greatness of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arm they became still as stone, until {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people passed over, O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, until the people that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} acquired passed over.

R.16: Terror and fear fell on them. Your great power made them as still as a rock until {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people passed by, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}. They stood still until the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had made {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own had passed by.

decisions.choice: the greatness of your arm: your great power
decisions.reason: The arm stands for strength. God promised to redeem Israel "with an outstretched arm" (6:6).

decisions.choice: passed over: crossed over, passed by
decisions.reason: The verb may mean passing through the lands of these peoples or crossing over the Jordan into Canaan (Joshua 3-4). The nations stand frozen with fear and do not stop them.

decisions.choice: acquired: gained as your own
decisions.reason: The verb means to get or acquire, often by buying. God has made Israel his own people (6:7; 19:5). The verb is also used of God as maker (Genesis 14:19, 22; Deuteronomy 32:6).

decisions.choice: made your own
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "acquired" here: Israel belongs to God.

records.source: תְּבִאֵ֗מוֹ וְתִטָּעֵ֨מוֹ֙ בְּהַ֣ר נַחֲלָֽתְךָ֔ מָכ֧וֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ֛ פָּעַ֖לְתָּ יְהוָ֑ה מִקְּדָ֕שׁ אֲדֹנָ֖י כּוֹנְנ֥וּ יָדֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: You will bring them and you will plant them on [the] mountain of your inheritance, [the] place for you to dwell [which] you have made, O Yahweh, [the] sanctuary, O my Lord, [which] have established your hands.
pieces: You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inheritance, the place {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have prepared for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} dwelling, O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, the sanctuary, O Lord, that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own hands set firm.

L.17: You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inheritance, [the] place for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to dwell [that] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made, O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, [the] sanctuary, O Lord, [that] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands have established.

R.17: You will bring {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people in and plant them on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own mountain. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, that is the place {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} home. Lord, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own hands built that holy place.

decisions.choice: plant them: settle them for good
decisions.reason: God's people are pictured as a tree planted to stay (2 Samuel 7:10; Psalm 80:9).

decisions.choice: the mountain of your inheritance: the land and the mountain that belong to God
decisions.reason: "Inheritance" is what is one's own to keep. The mountain may mean the hill country of Canaan as a whole (Deuteronomy 3:25; Psalm 78:54) or the mountain where God's sanctuary would stand, later Zion.

decisions.choice: the sanctuary, O Lord: the holy place God founds for himself
decisions.reason: The word means a holy place, the word used of the tabernacle in 25:8. "Lord" here is the title meaning master, not the divine name. God himself, not human builders, establishes it.

decisions.choice: your people
decisions.reason: Readable names whom God will bring in.

records.source: יְהוָ֥ה׀יִמְלֹ֖ךְ לְעֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃
records.gloss: Yahweh will reign forever and ever.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will reign forever and ever!"

L.18: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will reign forever and ever."

R.18: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will rule as king forever and ever!"

decisions.choice: will reign: will be king
decisions.reason: This is the first time the Bible says Yahweh reigns as king. Pharaoh's power is broken; Yahweh's rule has no end.

decisions.choice: forever and ever: for all time
decisions.reason: Two words for unending time are joined for force (Psalm 10:16).

decisions.choice: rule as king
decisions.reason: Readable spells out "reign".

records.source: כִּ֣י בָא֩ ס֨וּס פַּרְעֹ֜ה בְּרִכְבּ֤וֹ וּבְפָרָשָׁיו֙ בַּיָּ֔ם וַיָּ֧שֶׁב יְהוָ֛ה עֲלֵהֶ֖ם אֶת־מֵ֣י הַיָּ֑ם וּבְנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הָלְכ֥וּ בַיַּבָּשָׁ֖ה בְּת֥וֹךְ הַיָּֽם׃פ
records.gloss: For went [the] horse[s] of Pharaoh with his chariot[s] and with his horsemen into the sea, and brought back Yahweh on them the waters of the sea, and [the] sons of Israel walked on dry ground in [the] midst of the sea.
pieces: Pharaoh's horses, with his chariots and his horsemen, had gone into the sea, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had turned the sea's waters back on top of them; but the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had walked through the middle of the sea on dry ground.

L.19: For the horses of Pharaoh went with his chariots and with his horsemen into the sea, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought back the waters of the sea upon them, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel walked on dry ground in the midst of the sea.

R.19: This is what happened: Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and horsemen went into the sea, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the water flow back over them. But the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had walked across the sea on dry ground.

decisions.choice: for: this happened when ... a summary of the crossing
decisions.reason: The verse sums up 14:23-29 in prose after the song. It may give the reason for the song or set the scene for Miriam's singing.

decisions.choice: horse: Pharaoh's horses
decisions.reason: The singular stands for all of Pharaoh's horses, as in 14:9, 23.

decisions.choice: had gone ... had turned ... had walked (Balanced); This is what happened (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the verse as looking back. Readable opens with a phrase that shows it is a summary.

records.source: וַתִּקַּח֩ מִרְיָ֨ם הַנְּבִיאָ֜ה אֲח֧וֹת אַהֲרֹ֛ן אֶת־הַתֹּ֖ף בְּיָדָ֑הּ וַתֵּצֶ֤אןָ כָֽל־הַנָּשִׁים֙ אַחֲרֶ֔יהָ בְּתֻפִּ֖ים וּבִמְחֹלֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And took Miriam the prophetess, [the] sister of Aaron, the tambourine in her hand, and went out all the women after her with tambourines and with dances.
pieces: Miriam the prophetess, Aaron's sister, picked up a tambourine, and all the women came out behind her, beating tambourines and dancing.

L.20: And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took the tambourine in her hand, and all the women went out after her with tambourines and with dances.

R.20: Aaron's sister Miriam was a prophet. She took a tambourine in her hand. All the women followed her, playing tambourines and dancing.

decisions.choice: Miriam the prophetess: a woman who spoke for God
decisions.reason: Miriam is the first woman the Bible calls a prophet. Later Deborah and Huldah are called prophetesses (Judges 4:4; 2 Kings 22:14). God spoke through Miriam as well as Moses (Numbers 12:2; Micah 6:4).

decisions.choice: the sister of Aaron: and of Moses
decisions.reason: Miriam was the sister of Aaron and Moses (Numbers 26:59), most likely the sister who watched over the baby Moses (2:4, 7). She is named here with Aaron, perhaps because he was the elder brother.

decisions.choice: tambourines and dances: the women's victory celebration
decisions.reason: The instrument was a hand drum, a frame drum beaten by hand. Women went out with drums and dancing to welcome a victory (Judges 11:34; 1 Samuel 18:6).

decisions.choice: prophet
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer word "prophet" for a woman as for a man; Literal and Balanced say "prophetess".

records.heading: Miriam's song

records.source: וַתַּ֥עַן לָהֶ֖ם מִרְיָ֑ם שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָה֙ כִּֽי־גָאֹ֣ה גָּאָ֔ה ס֥וּס וְרֹכְב֖וֹ רָמָ֥ה בַיָּֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And answered them Miriam, sing to Yahweh, for highly he is exalted; horse and its rider he has thrown in [the] sea.
pieces: Miriam led them in the refrain: "Sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is lifted high in triumph; horse and rider {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has flung into the sea."

L.21: And Miriam answered them, "Sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for highly exalted is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}; horse and its rider {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has cast into the sea."

R.21: Miriam led them in singing: "Sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has won a great victory. He threw the horses and their riders into the sea."

decisions.choice: answered them: sang back to them, led them in response
decisions.reason: The verb means to answer, and in song to sing in response. Miriam and the women sing back, perhaps after each part of the song or as its refrain. "Them" is masculine, which may mean the whole people.

decisions.choice: the refrain of verse 1
decisions.reason: Miriam's words repeat the opening of the song (verse 1), with "Sing" in place of "I will sing".

decisions.choice: led them in the refrain (Balanced); led them in singing (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "answered" means here. Literal keeps "answered".

records.source: וַיַּסַּ֨ע מֹשֶׁ֤ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִיַּם־ס֔וּף וַיֵּצְא֖וּ אֶל־מִדְבַּר־שׁ֑וּר וַיֵּלְכ֧וּ שְׁלֹֽשֶׁת־יָמִ֛ים בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר וְלֹא־מָ֥צְאוּ מָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And led out Moses Israel from [the] Sea of Reeds, and they went out into [the] wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness and not they found water.
pieces: Moses had Israel move on from the Red Sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur. For three days they walked through the wilderness without coming upon any water.

L.22: And Moses led Israel out from the Sea of Reeds, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness and did not find water.

R.22: Then Moses led the Israelites away from the Red Sea into the Shur Desert. They walked for three days in the desert, and they did not find any water.

decisions.choice: led out: had the people set out, break camp
decisions.reason: The verb is used of pulling up tent pegs and setting out on a journey (12:37; 13:20).

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Shur: the desert east of Egypt
decisions.reason: Shur lay on the eastern border of Egypt, on the way from Egypt toward Canaan (Genesis 16:7; 25:18; 1 Samuel 15:7).

decisions.choice: three days: the journey Moses had asked Pharaoh for
decisions.reason: Moses had asked to go "three days' journey" into the wilderness to sacrifice (3:18; 5:3). After three days the people find no water.

decisions.choice: the Red Sea
decisions.reason: As at 10:19 and 15:4. Literal says "Sea of Reeds".

records.heading: Bitter water at Marah

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ מָרָ֔תָה וְלֹ֣א יָֽכְל֗וּ לִשְׁתֹּ֥ת מַ֨יִם֙ מִמָּרָ֔ה כִּ֥י מָרִ֖ים הֵ֑ם עַל־כֵּ֥ן קָרָֽא־שְׁמָ֖הּ מָרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they came to Marah, and not they were able to drink water from Marah, for bitter [were] they; therefore one called its name Marah.
pieces: When they came to Marah, they could not drink the water there, because it was bitter. That is why the place was named Marah.

L.23: And they came to Marah, and they could not drink [the] water from Marah, for it [was] bitter; therefore its name was called Marah.

R.23: They came to a place called Marah. They could not drink the water there because it was bitter. That is why the place is called Marah, which means "bitter."

decisions.choice: Marah: "bitter"
decisions.reason: The name Marah means bitter, and is from the same root as "bitter" in this verse. Naomi takes the name Mara for her bitter grief (Ruth 1:20).

decisions.choice: one called its name: it was named
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject: people called it so.

decisions.choice: which means "bitter"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name, which makes the point of the verse.

records.source: וַיִּלֹּ֧נוּ הָעָ֛ם עַל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹ֖ר מַה־נִּשְׁתֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And grumbled the people against Moses, saying, what will we drink?
pieces: The people grumbled at Moses. "What are we going to drink?" they said.

L.24: And the people grumbled against Moses, saying, "What will we drink?"

R.24: The people grumbled to Moses. "What will we drink?" they asked.

decisions.choice: grumbled: complained, murmured in discontent
decisions.reason: The verb means to complain against someone. This is the first of Israel's complaints in the wilderness (16:2, 7-8; 17:3; Numbers 14:2), against Moses and so against God (16:8).

decisions.choice: What will we drink?: three days after the sea
decisions.reason: The people who sang of God's power three days before now ask what they will drink. Their question is a complaint, not a request.

records.source: וַיִּצְעַ֣ק אֶל־יְהוָ֗ה וַיּוֹרֵ֤הוּ יְהוָה֙ עֵ֔ץ וַיַּשְׁלֵךְ֙ אֶל־הַמַּ֔יִם וַֽיִּמְתְּק֖וּ הַמָּ֑יִם שָׁ֣ם שָׂ֥ם ל֛וֹ חֹ֥ק וּמִשְׁפָּ֖ט וְשָׁ֥ם נִסָּֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And he cried out to Yahweh, and showed him Yahweh a tree, and he threw [it] into the waters, and became sweet the waters. There he made for him a statute and a rule, and there he tested him.
pieces: Moses cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} pointed him to a piece of wood. He threw it into the water, and the water turned sweet. It was there that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} laid down a statute and a rule for them, and there that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put them to the test.

L.25: And he cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} showed him a tree, and he threw [it] into the water, and the water became sweet. There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made for them a statute and a rule, and there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} tested them.

R.25: Moses cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} showed him a piece of wood. Moses threw it into the water, and the water became good to drink. There {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the people a rule and a law to live by. And there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} tested them.

decisions.choice: showed him a tree: pointed out, taught him about a piece of wood
decisions.reason: The word means a tree or a piece of wood. The verb "showed" is the verb for teaching or instructing: God taught Moses what to do. The healing came from God, not from the wood.

decisions.choice: there he made for them a statute and a rule: God, for Israel
alternatives: there Moses made for them a statute and a rule
decisions.reason: "He" is most likely Yahweh, who speaks in verse 26 and who tests Israel again in 16:4. The pronoun "him" is singular in Hebrew; it means the people as one body.

decisions.choice: tested them: proved them, to show what was in their hearts
decisions.reason: God tests his people to show whether they will trust and obey him (16:4; 20:20; Deuteronomy 8:2). The test is the condition in verse 26.

decisions.choice: Moses ... the LORD
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who cries out and who makes the statute; the Hebrew says only "he". Literal keeps "he".

decisions.choice: a rule and a law to live by
decisions.reason: Readable says "rule" for "statute", as elsewhere in Exodus, and "law" for the second word.

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אִם־שָׁמ֨וֹעַ תִּשְׁמַ֜ע לְק֣וֹל׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ וְהַיָּשָׁ֤ר בְּעֵינָיו֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְהַֽאֲזַנְתָּ֙ לְמִצְוֺתָ֔יו וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֖ כָּל־חֻקָּ֑יו כָּֽל־הַמַּֽחֲלָ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־שַׂ֤מְתִּי בְמִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לֹא־אָשִׂ֣ים עָלֶ֔יךָ כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה רֹפְאֶֽךָ׃ס
records.gloss: And he said, if surely you listen to [the] voice of Yahweh your God, and the right in his eyes you do, and you give ear to his commandments and you keep all his statutes, any of the sickness which I put on Egypt not will I put on you, for I [am] Yahweh [who] heals you.
pieces: He said, "If you listen closely to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sees as right, if you pay heed to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands and keep all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes, I will spare you every one of the sicknesses that I laid on the Egyptians. For I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who heals you."

L.26: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "If you will surely listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and do what is right in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes, and give ear to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments, and keep all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes, none of the sicknesses that I put on Egypt will I put on you, for I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [who] heals you."

R.26: He said, "Listen carefully to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says is right. Pay attention to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands, and obey all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rules. If you do, I will not make you suffer any of the diseases I sent on the Egyptians. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the one who heals you."

decisions.choice: if you will surely listen: if you listen with care
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for force: real listening that leads to obeying.

decisions.choice: the sicknesses I put on Egypt: the plagues
decisions.reason: God means the plagues, such as the boils (9:8-12). God will not treat obedient Israel as he treated Egypt (Deuteronomy 7:15; 28:27, 60).

decisions.choice: I am Yahweh who heals you: healing is God's work
decisions.reason: God names himself by what he does for Israel. He has just made bitter water sweet; he heals his people. God speaks of himself first by name ("Yahweh your God") and then as "I".

decisions.choice: Listen ... If you do
decisions.reason: Readable turns the long "if" sentence into commands followed by the promise.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אֵילִ֔מָה וְשָׁ֗ם שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֛ה עֵינֹ֥ת מַ֖יִם וְשִׁבְעִ֣ים תְּמָרִ֑ים וַיַּחֲנוּ־שָׁ֖ם עַל־הַמָּֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And they came to Elim, and there [were] twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees; and they camped there by the water.
pieces: Next they arrived at Elim. Twelve springs of water were there, and seventy palm trees, and they set up camp beside the water.

L.27: And they came to Elim, and there [were] twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees; and they camped there by the water.

R.27: Next the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} came to a place called Elim. It had twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees. So they camped there by the water.

decisions.choice: Elim: an oasis with springs and palms
decisions.reason: After the bitter water of Marah, Israel comes to a place with plenty of water and shade. Israel camps at Elim again in Numbers 33:9, which gives the same numbers.

decisions.choice: the Israelites
decisions.reason: Readable names the people who came to Elim.
